Proposed Methodology

5

The components and steps involved in our pipeline :


  • Base Model : Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct

  • LoRA Fine-tuning : Parameter efficient method that trains only 4.7M parameters (r=8, α=16) instead of the full model

  • Rollout Generation : For each chart-question pair, the model generates 8 candidate responses with moderate randomness

  • Parsing : Each generated response is decomposed into four parts - predicted chart type, extracted table values, reasoning trace, and final answer.

  • Filtering : A rollout is kept in the “fully correct” set only if its chart type, extracted table, and final answer all match ground truth, preventing lucky
    guesses from being rewarded.

  • Rewards : The total reward consists of three individual rewards

    • Chart RVR rewards ( R_base ) : Each individual response receives a base reward for correctness and structure, scoring things like format,
      chart type, table extraction, reasoning quality, final answer, and response length.

    • Hierarchical Correct-Path Consistency (HCPC) : A cross-rollout reward that encourages consistent chart-type prediction, consistent table
      extraction, and diverse reasoning paths among the rollouts that are fully correct.

    • Cross-Level Coherence (CLC) : Checks whether the numbers mentioned in the reasoning actually come from the extracted table

  • Policy Update :

    • GRPO : A policy update rule that compares each rollout’s reward to the group average and boosts above-average responses while suppressing
      below-average ones.

    • NSR :A training variant that skips reinforcement on correct samples and only penalizes wrong ones, which helps preserve multiple valid
      reasoning strategies instead of collapsing to one.

    • W REINFORCE : A hybrid update rule that gives weak positive reinforcement to correct responses and strong negative reinforcement to
      wrong ones, aiming to balance accuracy and diversity.

  • Gradient Update : Update the model so higher-quality responses become more likely.

Model: Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct

Platforms Used: Kaggle and Local PC

Hardware:

  • NVIDIA H100 40GB (Kaggle)

  • NVIDIA RTX 3090 24GB VRAM (Local PC)


Frameworks Used:

  • transformers + trl — model loading and GRPO training loop

  • peft — LoRA adapter integration

  • bitsandbytes — bf16 mixed-precision training

  • vllm — fast batch inference for evaluation


Training Duration: ~10 hours per method with ~8 hours on evaluation

The main navigation contains buttons for document level options. To switch between buttons, use the left and right keys and to activate, press Enter. To skip to the canvas, press “Ctrl+F2”.

The canvas is where your design is. To navigate into the page, press Enter. To navigate into groups or elements on the page, press Enter again. Press tab to move to the next page, group, or element. To operate the toolbar, use the “Ctrl+F1” key. If an element is selected, move it using the arrow keys; rotate using the “,” key and “.” key; and resize using the arrow keys with the “Ctrl” key. The side panel is where you can apply templates or add elements. To skip to the canvas, press “Ctrl+F2”.
